records.name: Bella Vista Neighbors Association
records.summary: Bella Vista Neighbors Association is one of the community organizations registered with the City to review nearby zoning and building proposals in the Central part of the city. Neighbors can follow what is planned and speak up.
records.what_you_do: Join a volunteer committee such as zoning, public safety, beautification, transportation, or climate, or come to meetings when they are announced. The zoning committee hosts community reviews of nearby variances, development, liquor licenses, and sidewalk cafes.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: Palumbo Recreation Center, 700 S 9th Street Philadelphia, PA 19147

first_step.how: Email info@bellavistaneighbors.org and ask to be connected with the chair of a committee you care about.
first_step.basis: The site lists its committees and says how to join: email the office or call and be introduced to a chair. Meetings are announced, but the site gives no days or times.
first_step.what_to_expect: Everything here is volunteer-run, and the site does not say when committees meet. Most people start by emailing the office, then talk with the chair of the committee they pick. The zoning committee is the one that hosts community reviews of nearby projects.
first_visit_tips: Email info@bellavistaneighbors.org before you come, since the site does not post meeting times.
Ask which committee meets soonest, and ask the chair for the place and time.

records.notes: Deep pass 2026-10-08. Status changed from active to dormant. The group's own newest dated items are a March 2021 e-news issue and 2022 items dated by year only (a Summer 2022 committee and 2022 bylaws), so the newest dated evidence is more than 24 months old. The 2026 City registry entry is the only current signal and is not counted as group activity. Confirm with the group before treating it as active. The Palumbo Recreation Center meeting place is carried from the City list; the group's site does not name it. Sidewalk sweeping is done by paid workers, not residents, so it is not described as volunteer work. Founded 1992 as a town watch, incorporated 1994, renamed 2014. The site says the group is non-partisan. Membership is not defined and no dues are listed; joining means emailing the office.

records.name: Black Pearl Chamber Orchestra
records.summary: A Philadelphia chamber orchestra that plays concerts and runs hands-on programs: a conducting class for young people, open rehearsals, and a leadership session for business teams.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket for a concert on the performances page, attend an open rehearsal when one is scheduled, or join a program. iConduct! is for young people in Philadelphia public schools. Orchestrating Leadership is a live rehearsal for executives and their teams, led by the conductor.

schedule.text: Concerts are posted on the performances page as they are scheduled. Each concert page gives its time and venue.

locations.label: Office (Graham Building)
locations.address: Graham Building, 30 South 15th Street, 15th Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19102

cost.text: Tickets are sold online for each concert. Prices are not listed on the homepage or the concert page.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for a concert listed on the performances page, or email michele@blackpearlco.org to ask when the next open rehearsal is.
first_step.basis: Concerts are open to anyone, and the ticket route is clear online. The open rehearsal welcomes all ages, but the site gives no dates or place, so you must email to ask.
first_step.what_to_expect: A concert is a ticketed performance, and you buy tickets online before you go. At an open rehearsal you watch musicians work through the music and see how the conductor leads. Sometimes audience members get to conduct the orchestra live.
first_visit_tips: Buy concert tickets online through the link on the concert page.
Email michele@blackpearlco.org before an open rehearsal to confirm the date and place.

records.notes: Deep pass 2026-10-08. The December 20, 2026 concert at 4 pm is a one-time event, so it is kept out of the schedule text and shows only as the last sign of life. Ticket prices are not published. The open rehearsal has no dates, place, cost, or accessibility notes on the site; the route is to email michele@blackpearlco.org. iConduct! started in 2009 (month not given) and meets in Philadelphia public schools. Orchestrating Leadership is for executives and their teams, with contact through jeri@blackpearlco.org. The concert partner choir is listed as a lead.

records.name: Callowhill Neighborhood Association
records.summary: Callowhill Neighborhood Association is one of the community organizations registered with the City to review nearby zoning and building proposals in the Central part of the city. Neighbors can follow what is planned and speak up.
records.what_you_do: Pay yearly dues to join, then get neighborhood emails about zoning, public meetings, and events. The group reviews nearby zoning and building proposals and shares its view with the City and developers.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: Philly House, 302 N 13th St and FACTS Charter School 1023 Callowhill St

cost.text: Yearly dues: $30 individual, $15 associate for people who live or work outside the neighborhood, and $60 corporate. Pay online or by check.

first_step.how: Sign up for the neighborhood emails on callowhill.org, then ask the group for the next meeting date before you pay dues.
first_step.basis: Membership is open and the dues are listed, but the site does not say when meetings happen or what members do, so you must pay or ask before you can see what it is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe meetings, volunteer roles, or events. You join by paying yearly dues online or by check, and you can sign up for neighborhood emails about zoning, public meetings, and events. Ask the group for the next meeting date before you pay.
first_visit_tips: Ask the group where and when meetings are held, since the site does not say.
If you pay by check, make it out to the association and note on the memo line that it is for annual dues.

records.notes: Deep pass 2026-10-08. Status changed from active to dormant. The group's own newest dated items are annual financial statements for 2020 to 2022, shown by year only, and no meeting, event, or news dates are posted. last_sign_of_life is deliberately not set because no month can be established; the tier 1 value of 2026-10 came from the City registry and should be cleared. Contact email changed from the City list personal address (sarahmceneaney@me.com) to the group's published address, callowhill@gmail.com. The phone number is carried from the City list because the site does not publish one. The Philly House and FACTS meeting place is carried from the City list and is not named on the group's site. Membership levels are individual, associate, and corporate. The Google Drive folder of meeting minutes was not opened.

records.name: Center City Organized for Responsible Development
records.summary: Center City Organized for Responsible Development is a Registered Community Organization (RCO) in the Central part of the city. The City asks developers to talk with RCOs about nearby zoning and building plans, so this is a way for neighbors to have a say.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come together to review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers.

locations.label: Contact address (City list)
locations.address: Arch Street United Methodist Church, 55 N. Broad St., Philadelphia, PA 19107

first_step.how: Email ccordphilly@gmail.com to ask about the next meeting and how to take part.
first_step.basis: We could not read the group's own pages, so how to take part is not yet confirmed. Only a contact email and an online meeting link from the City list are known.

records.name: Center City Residents Association (CCRA)
records.summary: A neighborhood group the City of Philadelphia has registered to be consulted on zoning and development in the Central part of the city, Center City Residents Association (CCRA) gives neighbors a place to hear about projects and respond.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area. Members who serve on the Zoning Committee review posted project materials, visit proposed project sites, and attend the monthly meeting.

schedule.text: The Zoning Committee meets monthly on the 4th Tuesday at 7 pm. Meetings are open to the public and are currently held by Zoom.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: BEX Meeting Space, 2005 Market St, and via Zoom

first_step.how: Attend the Zoning Committee meeting, held on the 4th Tuesday of the month at 7 pm by Zoom and open to the public.
first_step.basis: The monthly zoning meetings are open to the public. Joining the committee itself needs CCRA membership and a short resume, which is less casual.
first_step.what_to_expect: Zoning Committee meetings are held monthly by Zoom on the 4th Tuesday at 7 pm and are open to the public. Committee members review project materials before each meeting, and the co-chairs call on people in turn. The site does not say how long a meeting lasts or how many people usually attend.
first_visit_tips: Read the agendas and reports page first to see which projects are on the list.
Keep comments to zoning code and quality of life topics, and wait for the co-chair to call on you.
To sit on the committee, send a short resume and a statement of interest by email; you must be a CCRA member first.

records.notes: Deep pass 2026-10-08. The Zoning Committee is the only committee listed. It meets monthly on the 4th Tuesday at 7 pm, open to the public, currently by Zoom. The agendas page lists 2026 reports through September and says the October item is still to be posted. The Zoom link is not published here. Membership dues are not published, so no cost is given. The board minutes page returned a member login form; we did not log in. The group's site also says it manages the Schuylkill River Park Community Garden, which is listed as a lead. The residential membership levels are individual, under 40, senior, household, and three higher tiers.

records.name: Central Delaware Advocacy Group (CDAG)
records.summary: If you care about what gets built near you, Central Delaware Advocacy Group (CDAG) is a City registered community organization in the Central part of the city that hears about zoning and development proposals.
records.what_you_do: A volunteer coalition of civic and nonprofit groups that follows waterfront and zoning plans for the Central Delaware and talks them over at a monthly public meeting.

schedule.text: Meets in person on the second Thursday of each month, 6 to 7:30 pm, at the Society Hill Towers Community Room.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: Society Hill Towers Community Room, 216 St James Place, Philadelphia, PA 19106

cost.text: No membership dues. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Email info.cdag@gmail.com to confirm the next monthly meeting is still on, then come to the second Thursday meeting at 6 pm.
first_step.basis: Meetings are open to the public and the group lists a clear contact address. The newest dated post on the site is from 2021, so confirm the meeting is still happening before you go.
first_step.what_to_expect: The meeting is in person, once a month on a Thursday evening, in the community room at Society Hill Towers. The group is a coalition that follows the Central Delaware waterfront and zoning plans, so expect talk about those projects. There are no dues, and optional donations are accepted. The site does not say how long a meeting runs.
first_visit_tips: Confirm the meeting is on before you go, since the newest dated post on the site is from 2021.
Arrive a little early to find the community room, which is near the mini market in Society Hill Towers.

records.notes: Deep pass 2026-10-08. Status changed from active to dormant. The newest dated post is August 11, 2021, and the minutes archive shows posts from 2017 only; no 2025 or 2026 items were found. The monthly meeting schedule is stated on the site but is not dated, so it is not counted as evidence of activity. The City registry (2026) is not counted either. Contact email changed from the City list personal address to the group's published address, info.cdag@gmail.com. The phone number is carried from the City list because the site does not publish one. The Facebook page is linked on the site but was not read. The member organizations page is listed as a lead.

records.name: City of Brotherly Love Softball League
records.summary: A slow pitch softball league for LGBTQIA+ players and their allies. Divisions run from recreational to competitive, and the league offers new player clinics and social events.
records.what_you_do: Register for a season, get placed in a division that matches your skill level, and join a team. Each team has its own manager, and jerseys cost extra.

schedule.text: Play runs in seasons, including a fall season and a regular season.

locations.label: Fall Ball field: FDR Park
locations.address: Broad Street and Pattison Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19145

cost.text: Player fee of about $65 covers league play, field upkeep, and umpires. Jerseys cost extra.

first_step.how: Register for the current season on the league's registration page, or email join@cblsl.org to ask which division fits you.
first_step.basis: The league says all skill levels are welcome, from beginners to advanced players, and it runs new player clinics, though the site gives no clinic dates. You can register online or email to ask how to start.
first_step.what_to_expect: You sign up for a season, pay a player fee of about $65, and get placed on a team in a division that fits your skill level. The fee covers league play, field upkeep, and umpires, and jerseys cost extra. The site does not describe what a first game or practice is like, so ask the league before your first game.
first_visit_tips: Ask join@cblsl.org which division fits your skill level before you register.
Plan to buy your own jersey, which costs extra and is set by your team manager.
Fall Ball games are at FDR Park, entered from Pattison Avenue just west of Broad Street.

records.notes: Deep pass 2026-10-08. The cblsl.org address redirects to the league's LeagueApps site, which was read. Fall Ball 2026 registration is open. The end of season banquet on September 19, 2026 is the newest dated item. The fee of about $65 is from the league's about page; check the current season's registration for the exact amount. The fields page carries older permit text (2014), so the Dairy Fields and Edgely Fields listed there as regular season sites are not included until confirmed, and FDR Park should be confirmed too. The site has no FAQ or new player page. Age limits and gender rules are not stated. The ratings guidelines page and the partnership page were not read.
